title: Potain topless cranes help build world-record Yangtze River bridge in China
summary: Two Potain MCT 560 M25 tower cranes are building the south tower of the Shituo Yangtze River Bridge in Chongqing, China.The bridge will be the longest road-rail cable-stayed bridge with a split main span.Operating nearly 300 m above the Yangtze River, the cranes play a critical role in this major high-speed rail project.
body_markdown:
“The Potain MCT 560 M25 delivers outstanding performance at height, climbing to over 200 m with a 25 t maximum capacity,” said Leo Qian, marketing manager for Manitowoc China. “These characteristics make it well suited to the demands of high-altitude operations and heavy component handling on the Shituo Yangtze River Bridge, providing reliable performance to complete this demanding project."


The two Potain MCT 560 M25 cranes belong to Chongqing Haohai Construction Equipment Leasing, which purchased them in 2020. Before being deployed to the Shituo Yangtze River Bridge project, the cranes established a proven track record on the Taiziping Wujiang River Bridge project, where they operated continuously from 2020 through 2024. This excellent performance gave Chongqing Haohai Construction Equipment Leasing the confidence to use the cranes on the Shituo Yangtze River Bridge.


“We believed that the cranes would be particularly well suited to the Shituo Yangtze River Bridge because of their high working height and their ability to continue climbing beyond 200 m. They also offer an impressive lifting capacity and deliver reliable performance in challenging conditions,” said Jin Zhongxue, general manager, Chongqing Haohai Construction Equipment.


The Shituo Yangtze River Bridge is expected to open at the end of 2026.
